items.title: Tony Pua spends 45 minutes at Bukit Aman over Pardons Board minutes leak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Damansara member of parliament Tony Pua spent 45 minutes having his statement recorded at Bukit Aman today over the alleged leak of Pardons Board meeting minutes concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest issue. Speaking to reporters outside the federal police headquarters, Pua, who was accompanied by his lawyer Haijan Omar, said investigators questioned him about a Facebook post dated Nov 18, in which he published several pages of the meeting minutes. Pua said investigators also asked whom he was referring to as the "king kleptocrat" in his Facebook post.

items.title: Onn Hafiz: Differences of opinion no excuse to insult Rulers
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: The Johor government has warned against politicising the royal institution, stressing that constitutional decisions must be respected and differences of opinion should never be used to justify insulting or defying the Rulers. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the state government would continue to defend the sovereignty of the royal institution, uphold the Constitution and reject all forms of disloyalty to the Rulers. "Differences of opinion are no excuse for defiance or insulting the royal institution," he said during the winding-up of the 2027 Johor Budget debate at the state assembly in Bangunan Sultan Ismail, Kota Iskandar, today.

items.title: Renewed US tariff threat puts Malaysian tech, automotive firms in the spotlight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian technology and automotive manufacturers could face pressure from the United States' (US) proposed additional tariffs of up to 18 per cent, with companies heavily reliant on the US market most vulnerable, said Apex Securities Bhd. Among semiconductor players, Unisem (M) Bhd has a US revenue exposure of about 45 per cent, followed by Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd at 20 per cent, while Pentamaster Corp Bhd and ViTrox Corp Bhd have relatively lower exposure of 10 to 20 per cent. Among the EMS players identified, EG Industries Bhd has the highest US revenue exposure at 81 per cent, followed by Aurelius Technologies Bhd at 52 to 59 per cent and VS Industry Bhd at 20 to 33 per cent.

items.title: Al-Salam Reit's Q3 earnings jump 66pct on higher rental income, lower financing costs
items.summary: Quarterly revenue rose 4.8 per cent to RM23.29 million from RM22.23 million, while profit before tax increased 46.7 per cent to RM5.54 million from RM3.78 million. Revenue for the period increased 4.3 per cent to RM68.51 million from RM65.68 million, while profit before tax rose 71 per cent to RM17.25 million from RM10.09 million. Net property income for the nine-month period increased 6.8 per cent to RM47.8 million from RM44.7 million a year earlier.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz tells new Negeri Sembilan Exco to stay within their portfolios
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded newly appointed members of the state executive council (Exco) to remain within the scope of their respective portfolios and not overstep their authority and responsibilities. Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin Tuanku Muhriz. The ceremony was also attended by Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari; Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid; Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi; and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.

items.title: Tourists enjoy brilliant autumn colours in Kyoto
items.summary: KYOTO: Visitors from Japan and overseas marvelled at the brilliant reds and yellows of Kyoto's autumn foliage, as the season transformed the city's temples, gardens and mountains with a blaze of colour. The ancient Japanese capital is known for its cherry blossoms in spring, but autumn is another peak tourism season, particularly for local visitors keen to enjoy the centuries-old tradition of viewing vibrant autumn foliage. [[nid:1586917]] Kyoto has a long-standing tradition of appreciating autumn foliage.

items.title: Thunderstorms could crash Sarawak’s nomination day, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 27 — Most areas in Sarawak are expected to experience rain tomorrow, on the nomination day for the 13th Sarawak State Election. The Election Commission has set Dec 12 as the polling day for the 13th Sarawak State Election, with early voting scheduled for Dec 8. For the latest news on the 13th Sarawak State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/ .

items.title: Indonesia bourse suspends five firms over free-float data discrepancies
items.summary: JAKARTA: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Friday that it has suspended trading in the shares of five listed companies for failing to accurately report free-float share ownership data and for not correcting the discrepancies by the prescribed deadline. One company sanctioned by the bourse is PT MNC Tourism Indonesia, formerly known as MNC Land, a tourism company behind the Lido project affiliated with US President Donald Trump. MNC Tourism Indonesia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Anwar pays tribute to former attorney-general Abdul Gani Patail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the family of former attorney-general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail, who died last night. Gani was 71. Anwar said Gani remained steadfast during that difficult time until he was removed from office.

items.title: Abdul Gani Patail laid to rest in Presint 20
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Former attorney-general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail was laid to rest at the Presint 20 Muslim Cemetery here at 11.10am today. Among those present were Attorney-General (A-G) Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, former Umno Wanita chief Tan Sri Shahrizat Jalil, former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Abdul Hamid Bador and former Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Dr Mohd Irwan Serigar Abdullah. His second child, Faezul Adzra Patail Abdul Gani, confirmed the death when contacted yesterday.

items.title: Malaysia's producer prices rise 14pct in October as mining costs surge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Producer Price Index (PPI) for local production rose 14.0 per cent year-on-year in October 2026, accelerating from 12.0 per cent in September, the Statistics Department said. The mining sector recorded the steepest increase of 75.4 per cent in October, compared with 54.1 per cent in the preceding month. Taiwan recorded the highest increase among the selected economies at 19.7 per cent, followed by Denmark (13.0 per cent), India (12.3 per cent), Thailand (10.2 per cent), the United States (6.5 per cent) and China (5.7 per cent).

items.title: PBS signals readiness to contest Kota Kinabalu parliamentary seat
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: PBS has declared its readiness to contest the Kota Kinabalu parliamentary seat in the next general election. PBS Luyang division chief Goon Tien Shang said the party had a longstanding presence in Kota Kinabalu, having served the community since its establishment in 1985. PBS Likas division chief Soo Chee Yong said unity and cooperation among the three divisions would strengthen the party's preparations.

items.title: Smiling, silent, says will talk later: Tony Pua walks into Bukit Aman to explain his Najib Facebook post
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Tony Pua turned up at Bukit Aman today to answer to police over 55 reports lodged against his Facebook post on the Pardons Board minutes concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest. The former Damansara MP reached the federal police headquarters with his lawyer at about 9.53am, smiled at reporters without commenting and said he would speak after giving his statement, the New Straits Times reported. Yesterday, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police received 55 complaints over Pua’s remarks and two over Khoo’s.

items.title: RTD: Low wages drive Penang lorry drivers to overload by up to 90pct
items.summary: SEBERANG JAYA: Low basic wages are driving commercial lorry drivers in Penang to overload their vehicles by up to 90 per cent to earn additional commissions, the Road Transport Department (RTD) says. Penang RTD director Zulkifly Ismail said transport operators often linked drivers' commissions directly to the volume of cargo carried, encouraging them to maximise loads and make more trips at the expense of road safety. "To earn these commissions, drivers routinely carry excessive loads and chase trips for higher pay," he told reporters at the state RTD headquarters after an early-morning operation targeting overloaded commercial vehicles.

items.title: Penang leads Malaysia's export growth with 109.3pct surge in October
items.summary: The state accounted for 51.9 per cent of Malaysia's total exports, followed by Johor at 19 per cent and Selangor at 11.9 per cent. Malaysia's total trade rose to RM436.6 billion in October, comprising exports of RM239.2 billion and imports of RM197.4 billion. Meanwhile, imports rose by RM69.5 billion, or 54.4 per cent, year-on-year, with Penang recording the largest increase of RM34.7 billion, followed by Johor (RM20.4 billion) and Selangor (RM5.2 billion).

items.title: Borneo to prosper with IKEA's uniform nationwide pricing
items.summary: IKEA, the well-known Swedish home-furnishing giant, creates history this week when it opens its first store in East Malaysia and, indeed, the first in the entire island of Borneo, in Kuching. Ikea has committed to offering its products in Kuching at the same prices as those charged in all its other stores in the country, without the premiums that Malaysians outside the peninsula are long used to paying. Takeshi Murai, Ikea Malaysia's country retail director, related to the media last month that Kuching was selected after the company considered the city's potential, conducted market research and assessed the practical arrangements needed to serve customers at affordable prices.

items.title: Tony Pua gives statement to police over Najib pardon minutes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: : Former Damansara MP Tony Pua arrived at Bukit Aman to have his statement recorded over a Facebook post on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest pardon minutes. https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/1584984/igp-tony-pua-may-be-summoned-over-leaked-pardons-board-meeting-minutes#google_vignette Pua said he would address the media after giving his statement at Bukit Aman. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police had received 55 reports over Pua's Facebook post concerning the minutes of a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting involving Najib.

items.title: Six new Negeri Sembilan exco members sworn in as Ismail Lasim stays on as MB
items.summary: Berita Harian reported that the swearing-in ceremony took place at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah, where Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim announced the six appointments approved by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Umno’s three representatives are Kota assemblyman Suhaimi Aini, Senaling assemblyman Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil and Jeram Padang assemblyman Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir. In September, the previous councillors backed a proclamation naming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as ruler in place of Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Religious affairs minister demands apology from radio station over clip resembling Islamic prayer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan has urged the management of a private radio station to immediately remove a viral video linking Islamic prayer (solat) to English Premier League football matches and issue a public apology to the Muslim community. In a statement posted on Facebook today, Zulkifli also called on the radio station to issue a public apology to the Muslim community and ensure that a similar incident does not recur. Recently, an 11-second video titled “Praying for Man United”, uploaded by a radio station, went viral on social media.

items.title: MB: Johor councillors, village chiefs face annual KPI reviews or risk losing posts
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor plans to shorten the appointment terms of village chiefs and local councillors from two years to one, with reappointments subject to their performance against key performance indicators (KPIs). Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the proposed move was aimed at strengthening accountability and ensuring community leaders remained responsive to residents' needs. He said their performance would be assessed based on their engagement with residents, response times to public complaints and the effectiveness of follow-up action.

items.title: Sarawak polls: EC seeks A-GC's advice on possible GPS majority tomorrow
items.summary: KUCHING: The Election Commission (EC) is seeking clarification from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) on the legal implications should Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secure a simple majority to form the state government after the nomination process for the 13th Sarawak state election concludes tomorrow. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the matter was still being reviewed by the A-GC to ensure that any action or decision taken complied with existing election regulations. He said that under the current regulations, all stipulated election processes must proceed, while any announcement on the matter would only be made after the EC received confirmation from the relevant authorities.

items.title: Storms on the way: Penang tells all districts to get disaster committees ready
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 27 — Penang housing and environment executive councillor Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu has directed all district officers to activate their disaster management committees as forecasts warn of thunderstorms in most areas of the state tomorrow afternoon. Sundarajoo said the Penang State Disaster Management Committee issued the directive to ensure districts could monitor flood risks and coordinate quickly with the agencies involved. Rain and thunderstorms may also occur in some areas at night.

items.title: Boy killed in Pasir Mas crash helped mother deliver kuih
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Ten-year-old Muhammad Saiful Haider Saiful Nizam was always eager to help his mother deliver homemade kuih to a nearby food stall before going to school. The crash killed Haider and his six-year-old brother, Muhammad Saiful Hayyan, while their eldest brother, Muhammad Saiful Haikal, was injured. Food stall owner Mohd Rosli Awang Ngah said Haider would deliver the kuih prepared by his mother, known among locals as Anis, before school and return in the evening to collect payment from the sales.

items.title: [UPDATED] 6 new Negri Sembilan exco members appointed
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has appointed six state executive council (Exco) members, paving the way for the state administration to be re-established after a prolonged crisis lasting nearly four months. Also present was the Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud. They are Kota assemblyman Suhaimi Aini, Senaling assemblyman Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil, Jeram Padang assemblyman Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir and Repah assemblyman Koh Kim Swee.

items.title: RHB Research upgrades Syarikat Takaful to 'Buy' on stronger-than-expected earnings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Research has upgraded its call on Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Bhd to "Buy" from "Neutral" after the company's nine-month earnings exceeded expectations. The company's third-quarter net profit of RM218 million brought its nine-month earnings to RM318 million, accounting for 81 per cent of the research firm's full-year estimate and 80 per cent of the consensus forecast. The firm noted that Syarikat Takaful's underwriting margin rebounded to 9.4 per cent in the third quarter from 1.3 per cent in the preceding quarter.

items.title: Ismail Lasim turns up at Seri Menanti as Negeri Sembilan exco swearing-in gets under way nearly four months into crisis
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim arrived at Istana Besar Seri Menanti today for the swearing-in of the state executive council (exco), Harian Metro reported. Yesterday, Tuanku Muhriz received several BN leaders in audience at Istana Hinggap in Seremban. They were Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi; deputy chairman and Negeri Sembilan BN chief Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan; Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki; and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Onn Hafiz urges Putrajaya to return 25pc of Johor’s tax revenue
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 27 — The Johor state government has made a fresh call for the return of at least 25 per cent of the tax revenue contributed to the federal administration in order to strengthen the development of local facilities. He said the state government is currently assisting in the provision and upgrading of various facilities belonging to federal agencies, even though such matters do not fall under the state’s primary responsibilities. In December 2024, the Johor government formally requested that 20 per cent of the said tax revenue be channelled back to the state, providing the state with greater fiscal space to pursue development initiatives.

items.title: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
items.summary: Spot gold climbed 1.6 per cent to US$3,622.91 per ounce by 0247 GMT after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 on Wednesday, following hot US inflation data that cemented interest-rate-hike bets. US gold futures for December delivery gained 2.6 per cent to US$3,621.10. Among other metals, spot silver climbed 4.6 per cent to US$43.40, platinum gained 2.6 per cent to US$1,323.78, and palladium rose 3.3 per cent to US$901.50.

items.title: Onn Hafiz: BKJ Phase 7 extended to senior citizens, cancer patients, smallholders
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: More than 435,000 Johoreans will benefit from over RM90 million in additional assistance under three new categories of Bantuan Kasih Johor (BKJ) Phase 7, which will begin in June next year. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the RM200 cash aid would be given to senior citizens, cancer and dialysis patients, as well as B40 smallholders. He said the additional allocation reflected the state government's commitment to addressing public feedback and ensuring vulnerable groups were not overlooked.

items.title: Oriental Kopi shares jump 13.5pct to six-week high on stronger earnings
items.summary: For the fourth quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q4 FY26), the cafe chain operator booked a net profit of RM20.43 million, up 28.60 per cent from RM15.89 million a year earlier. Quarterly revenue rose 28.52 per cent to RM171.14 million from RM133.16 million, supported by its cafe chain operations and the distribution and retail of packaged food. For the full financial year ended Sept 30, 2026 (FY26), net profit increased 14.42 per cent to RM69.51 million from RM60.75 million, while revenue climbed 36.20 per cent to RM614.22 million from RM450.92 million.

items.title: What Malaysian listed companies look for in independent directors
items.summary: Boards look for relevant expertise, independent judgement and enough time to do the work. Media Prima Bhd group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali is among eight Malaysian executives whose careers illustrate what listed-company boards look for in independent directors. Before becoming Media Prima Bhd group managing director in October 2021, Datuk Rafiq Razali co-founded KFit and helped expand Media Prima's digital business.

items.title: Johor won't sacrifice people's well-being for investments, says MB
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor's 19 operational data centres have been approved to use 21 million litres of treated water daily, Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said. This represents just 1.05 per cent of the state's average daily treated water production of 2,034 million litres. Onn Hafiz said the state would not compromise water security, electricity supply or environmental sustainability in its efforts to attract investments.

items.title: MACC pushes back against ‘double standard’ claims, says facts guide probes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today firmly denied allegations that it applies a “double standard” in its investigations, including those involving government ministries. In a statement issued today, the MACC described the allegations as baseless, saying they did not reflect the principles of professionalism, integrity, and established procedures governing its investigations. The commission said it had initiated an investigation on Oct 7 into expenditure related to the Rural Road Project (JALB), which involves a government ministry.

items.title: MCMC serves Google in RM600m lawsuit, says YouTube failed to curb harmful content
items.summary: She said this was MCMC’s first lawsuit against Google. On Nov 25, MCMC announced two lawsuits against Google seeking RM600 million in total damages. MCMC is seeking RM300 million in each suit: RM100 million in general damages, RM100 million in aggravated damages and RM100 million in exemplary damages.

items.title: Sarawak polls: Sibu's transformation can attract local youth to return to serve — Dr Annuar
items.summary: SIBU: The ongoing transformation of Sibu, driven by modern infrastructure development and efforts to strengthen its economy over the next five years, is expected to encourage more local professionals and youths to return, work, and settle in the city. Sarawak Deputy Minister for Education, Innovation and Talent Development Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee said three strategic initiatives, namely the proposed Sibu Economic Zone (SEZ), the redevelopment of Kampung Datuk, and the urban renewal of Bukit Assek, would serve as key catalysts for the city's transformation. "The main challenge in developing Sibu is attracting more professionals and young people, particularly locals, to work and settle here over the next five years.

items.title: Putrajaya targets algorithmic manipulation and unfair pricing in new e-Commerce Bill
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) is finalising an e-Commerce Bill to strengthen platform accountability and protect consumers from algorithmic manipulation and discriminatory pricing. KPDN said the law will emphasise transparency, accountability, and fairness, and require platforms to disclose pricing information that affects consumers’ purchasing decisions clearly. KPDN said the Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599), including the Consumer Protection (Electronic Trade Transactions) Regulations 2024, currently governs online transactions, tackling misleading trade practices and false representations.

items.title: Tears in court as six, including three RMAF officers, face death penalty over 96kg meth trafficking at Subang air base
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 27 — A relative wept in the courtroom today as three Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers and three civilians were charged with trafficking 96.2kg of suspected methamphetamine at the RMAF Subang Air Base, the New Straits Times (NST) reported. The six arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here under heavy police escort, with armed officers in balaclavas and tactical gear, the newspaper said. They were named as Lieutenant Amir Ariffudin Aminullah, 33; Lieutenant Muhammad Arief Fauzan Mohd Ali, 27; Captain Muhammad Amirul Faisall Rosdin, 34; Tan Sui Seng, 48; Nur Hanis Syafiqah Muhammed Amin, 28; and Afifah Amdas, 34.

items.title: Indonesia bourse sanctions five companies over free-float share data discrepancies
items.summary: JAKARTA: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Friday that it had sanctioned five listed companies for failing to accurately report free-float share ownership data and for not correcting the discrepancies by the prescribed deadline. The bourse did not specify what the sanctions were One company sanctioned by the bourse is PT MNC Tourism Indonesia, formerly known as MNC Land, a tourism company behind the Lido tourism project affiliated with US President Donald Trump MNC Tourism Indonesia did not immediately respond to a request for comment The bourse said it identified discrepancies in the calculation and reporting of free-float shares by several listed companies and subsequently directed them to verify their disclosures and submit corrective filings by a specified deadline The sanctions follow broader market reforms implemented by Indonesian authorities after global index provider MSCI warned that it could downgrade the $1.4 trillion economy to "standalone" status Indonesian authorities have spent much of the year trying to address MSCI's concerns, tightening disclosure requirements and laying out plans to raise minimum free floats Free-floating shares are those openly available for public trading and not held by large core holders such as company officials, long-term investors, or government bodies © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Cyberbullying case ends with warning as student apologises to teenage victim
items.summary: TAWAU, Nov 26 — An 18-year-old student who pleaded guilty to uploading a teenage girl’s photograph on social media with threatening captions was discharged with a warning by the Magistrate’s Court here today after personally apologising to the victim. The court also ordered the return of RM500 bail. Investigations found that the accused uploaded the victim’s photograph after reading a WhatsApp group conversation claiming that a friend’s cousin had been bullied by the victim and another individual.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 27, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower at 1,570 on Friday amid subdued market sentiment following Wall Street's closure for the Thanksgiving holiday. The FBM KLCI is expected to trade cautiously within the 1,560 to 1,575 range today. Easing US yields and resilient domestic corporate earnings are expected to support selective buying in banking, consumer and telecommunications stocks, while sentiment towards AI-related counters remains cautious.

items.title: Want Perak youths to stay in their hometowns? MB says plan first, remote working hubs later
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 27 — Introducing rural remote working hub programmes to encourage youths to remain or return to their hometowns needs comprehensive study and planning, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said today. He was replying to Simpang Pulai assemblyman Wong Chai Yi had asked whether or not the state government plans to introduce rental incentives, rural community housing or rural remote working hubs to encourage young people to remain in or return to their hometowns. He said the local economic landscape was the main catalyst in encouraging young people to remain in their respective villages.

items.title: Abdul Gani Patail, the prosecutor behind some of Malaysia’s most watched trials
items.summary: Among the high-profile prosecutions Abdul Gani handled were the corruption case involving former Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Joseph Pairin Kitingan in 1993 and the case involving the Al-Ma’unah militant group in 2000. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, who confirmed the news of his death, also extended his condolences to Abdul Gani’s family. Abdul Gani was also part of the prosecution team in the 2006 murder case involving Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu.

items.title: Malaysian executives in digital transformation and board governance
items.summary: Media Prima Bhd group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali is among six Malaysian business leaders with experience relevant to boardroom discussions on digital transformation and governance. Which Malaysian executives bring experience in large-scale digital transformation? How did Rafiq Razali help transform Media Prima's digital business?

items.title: Amir Hamzah urges public-listed firms to back RM3,400 living wage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The government has called on public-listed companies (PLCs) to adopt the RM3,400 living wage benchmark across their organisations. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said that fair and adequate wages would enable employees to meet their basic needs and maintain a decent standard of living. Amir Hamzah also said companies must invest in developing their workforce capabilities, particularly in data analytics, sustainability and environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, climate finance and digital finance.

items.title: Customs seize 86 electric bicycles worth RM268,279 in Klang Valley raids
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Customs seized 86 electric bicycles suspected of being imported without permits and Sirim approval during raids at nine premises in the Klang Valley from Oct 27 to 30. Kuala Lumpur Customs director Wan Norizan Wan Daud said the bicycles were believed to have been imported in parts to evade detection. He said the four-day operation, conducted with Sirim, targeted the sale of electric bicycles that did not meet import requirements.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia opens lower amid sentiment
items.summary: At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 4.01 points to 1,566.97 from Thursday's close of 1,570.98. The benchmark index opened 0.15 of-a-point lower at 1,570.83. In active trade, NexG Bina inched up half a sen to four sen, Zetrix AI, Ingenieur Gudang and AHB Holdings inched down half a sen each to 4.5 sen, 2.5 sen and 3.5 sen, respectively.

items.title: Blackouts and floods fail to derail Sabah’s 42,808 SPM candidates
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — All 42,808 candidates sitting for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination in Sabah since last Monday have not been affected by the electricity disruption affecting the state’s East Coast yesterday. Sabah Education Department director Abidin Marjan said the SPM examination had proceeded smoothly so far, despite challenges posed by the power outage along Sabah’s East Coast and flooding, particularly in the interior district of Sook. Eight districts along Sabah’s East Coast experienced power disruptions after Sabah Electricity detected an incident affecting electricity transmission to the areas at 6.04am.

items.title: Same RM1,000 lease for seven others, so why only KLSCAH? Lim Guan Eng asks MACC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today accused the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) of double standards for probing the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall’s (KLSCAH) land lease extension but not seven other organisations that received the same RM1,000 premium. “Clearly there was no special treatment for KLSCAH,” Lim, who is from DAP, said, pointing to the seven organisations that Yeoh had listed as receiving the same RM1,000 premium for 99-year extensions in Kuala Lumpur. The seven organisations are Yayasan Tuanku Bainun, Pertubuhan Bakti, Majlis Kebangsaan Pertubuhan-Pertubuhan Wanita Malaysia, Majlis Kebajikan Kanak-Kanak Malaysia, Persatuan Bulan Sabit Merah Malaysia, Persatuan Keturunan Chan She Shu Yuen Kuala Lumpur & Selangor and Persatuan Badminton Malaysia.

items.title: Temporary tower reaches Ranau as Sabah Electricity works to restore severed grid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — The components of the Emergency Restoration System (ERS) temporary tower arrived at the site of the collapsed transmission tower in Ranau this morning to restore the electricity supply line connecting Sabah’s West Coast and East Coast. Sabah Electricity said the lorry transporting the ERS temporary tower container arrived safely at the site of transmission tower T313 at 1.07am. Sabah Electricity is also stepping up all efforts to expedite the restoration of electricity supply to affected consumers following the collapse of transmission tower T313 in Ranau yesterday.

items.title: Croc No. 2 in a month: 10-foot female caught alive off Daro waters in Sarawak
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 27 — A female crocodile measuring approximately 10 feet in length was captured alive in the waters off Kampung Sedi, Daro, yesterday. Licensed crocodile hunter Jeffery Siew said the reptile initially broke free from a hook after being pulled onto the riverbank and attempted to escape into nearby bushes. Siew said this was the second crocodile caught in the area this month.

items.title: One tax authority? Not yet, says MoF as IRB, Customs stay separate
items.summary: The proposed restructuring is expected to improve national revenue collection efficiency, curb tax leakages and reduce compliance costs for the business community. However, MOF said the government would continue to strengthen governance and improve tax revenue collection through both agencies, including by sharing information and conducting joint enforcement operations. These measures would enhance efficiency and sustainability in tackling revenue leakages, it said.

items.title: GPS could walk into 44 Sarawak seats unopposed after PKR pulls out, says DAP youth leader
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 27 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) could potentially win as many as 44 state seats uncontested in the 13th Sarawak Election following PKR’s withdrawal, said Jordan Soo. The Democratic Action Party Socialist Youth Sarawak deputy chief said this would allow GPS to secure a sufficient majority to form the next state government on nomination day, before voters had even cast their ballots. “The upcoming Sarawak election is no longer merely a contest between political parties.

items.title: Anwar looks to delivery after Parliament signs off on RM510b Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The passage of Budget 2027 by the Dewan Rakyat yesterday marks an important step in the Madani Government’s efforts to improve the lives of the people. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in a Facebook post yesterday, said the budget also encompassed efforts to strengthen the country’s resilience and secure its future. The fifth budget under the Madani Government involves government allocations totalling RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments and RM14.2 billion in investments from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance (Incorporated) (MOF Inc) companies.

items.title: Sabah Electricity scrambles to reconnect East Coast after Ranau tower collapse, eyes Dec 2 recovery
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — Sabah Electricity has set a six-day timeframe to restore the 275-kilovolt (kV) electricity transmission line to Sabah’s East Coast, targeting full grid restoration by Dec 2 after transmission tower T313 in Ranau collapsed yesterday. The collapse of tower T313, detected at 6.04am, severed two transmission line circuits running from the West Coast to the East Coast of Sabah, disrupting electricity supply across eight districts and affecting 153,599 registered consumers. “We are targeting a six-day period to reconnect the affected grid; it could possibly be completed even earlier,” said Sabah Electricity Chairman Datuk Saadiah Aziz at a press conference at the Sabah Electricity Headquarters last night.

items.title: ‘Halfway aligned?’: Judge gives Sabah AG three days to say which side it’s on in NGO’s continental shelf suit against Putrajaya
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — High Court judge Datuk Alexander Siew How Wai gave the Sabah Attorney General’s Chambers three days to decide its exact position on Sabah Action Body Advocating Rights (Sabar) case against the Federal Government on the Continental Shelf. Sabah AG Datuk Brendon Soh responded that he would file another affidavit to clarify the Sabah government’s position. Soh had applied to include the Sabah government as an intervenor respondent “more aligned with Sabar’s position”.

items.title: Hej, Kuching! IKEA opens its first East Malaysia store at The Pines Mall today
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 27 — Sarawakians will soon be able to shop for IKEA home furnishing products locally as the Swedish retailer opens its first store in East Malaysia at The Pines Mall, Batu Kawa, today. IKEA Kuching store manager Pathmalingam Arumugam said the 3,634-square-metre outlet would offer approximately 5,180 home furnishing articles, with prices on par with those at IKEA stores in peninsular Malaysia. Located on the first floor of The Pines Mall, the store features a showroom, Markethall, selected take-home products, an IKEA Planning Studio, IKEA for Business and a grab-and-go IKEA Food section.

items.title: Former Attorney General Abdul Gani Patail dies at 71
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Former Attorney General Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail died last night. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, when contacted, confirmed the news. Abdul Gani, 71, a law graduate of Universiti Malaya (UM), was the first graduate of a local university to be appointed Attorney General.

items.title: From kampung boy to Seri Negara curator: The Khazanah scholar who made his late mother proud
items.summary: Tan said he was still studying for his A-levels when he came across the Khazanah Scholarship programme through an online search. “It’s actually rare, because not many scholarships in Malaysia offered support for studies in international relations,” he said. To Cambridge, then nation-building,” he said.

items.title: From remote Batang Rajang to luxury tables: Sarawak’s prized empurau commands up to RM2,500 per kg
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 26 — The landing of an empurau weighing over 12 kilogrammes at the premises of Sarawak wild fish supplier Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong here proves that the species is not merely an ordinary river catch, but a luxury commodity worth tens of thousands of ringgit. For Jeferry, 41, the business is not merely about chasing profits through trading exotic fish, but also ensuring that every bit of hard work by local fishermen receives a fair and lucrative return. Apart from empurau, Jeferry’s business premises located at Jalan Long Bridge also supply various other freshwater species including patin buah, tapah, jelawat, semah, tengadak, terubuk, sebarau, giant freshwater prawns (udang galah), ketutu, and baung.

items.title: Cybersecurity gets its own priority in Malaysia’s new National Security Policy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched the National Security Policy 2026–2030, outlining Malaysia’s security priorities for the next five years, with a new strategic focus on cybersecurity and technology. “Our approach and outlook towards security threats have changed. The National Security Policy 2026–2030 is a continuation of the previous 2021–2025 policy, which was based on the Comprehensive Security concept.
